JD Sports' Profit Falls on Sector Challenges
JD Sports Fashion reported lower profit for its fiscal first half as the U.K. company continues to deal with a difficult market backdrop, including downbeat consumer sentiment.

The sneaker and fashion retailer said profit before tax and adjusted items--a company-preferred metric--dropped to 282 million pounds ($376.3 million) for the six months ended Aug. 1 from 351 million pounds a year earlier. The result came ahead of analysts' views of 279 million pounds, according to a poll of analysts' estimates provided by the company.
Sales fell by 0.7% on an organic basis, as previously announced, which the company said was a resilient performance given the backdrop including cost-of-living pressures for consumers.

For the fiscal year as a whole, the group maintained its outlook of adjusted pretax profit between 700 million and 800 million pounds, which it lowered last month due to the underlying sales trends and promotions in the sector.
"While the trading environment remains tough, I am encouraged by the progress we are making and confident in our strategic execution," Chief Executive Regis Schultz said.
